articles.title: Canvas Hack Aftermath: Owner Instructure Reaches Deal With Hacker Group
articles.summary: Google confirms AI just broke the entire internet by creating zero-day exploits that bypass 2FA like it's a suggestion, not a security measure. Welcome to the future where machines pwn humans with algorithmic precision.

articles.title: Microsoft's MDASH AI System Finds 16 Windows Flaws Fixed in Patch Tuesday
articles.summary: An 18-year-old NGINX vulnerability finally crawled out of its coding cave to grant unauthenticated RCE to anyone who asks nicely. Sometimes the best exploits age like fine wine in forgotten codebases.

articles.title: Help EFF Solve an Issue That's Bigger than Creepy Ads
articles.summary: Microsoft's April patch bonanza: 167 vulnerabilities including a SharePoint zero-day and the deliciously-named 'BlueHammer' Windows Defender flaw. When your security software needs security software, you know it's Tuesday.

articles.title: Anti-DDoS Firm Heaped Attacks on Brazilian ISPs
articles.summary: Canvas gets schooled by cybercriminals who turned education platforms into their personal playground, disrupting classes nationwide. Nothing says 'permanent record' like having your student data held for ransom.

articles.title: California colleges went big on online learning tools. Then the worst happened
articles.summary: Instructure cuts a deal with ShinyHunters after 9,000+ schools got pwned through Canvas. Classic corporate response: pay the pirates and hope they pinky-promise to delete everything.

articles.title: Patch Tuesday, April 2026 Edition
articles.summary: Scattered Spider's 'Tylerb' pleads guilty to wire fraud after his SMS phishing campaign proved humans are still the weakest link in any security chain. Social engineering: it just works.

articles.title: Victory! End-to-End Encrypted RCS Comes to Apple and Android Chats
articles.summary: Instagram kills its barely-used end-to-end encryption feature, breaking promises faster than teenagers break ToS agreements. Meta's privacy commitments have shorter lifespans than mayflies.

articles.title: EFF Launches New Offline Campaign for Saudi Wikipedian Osama Khalid
articles.summary: Victory dance time: Apple finally enables E2E encryption for RCS, meaning iPhone-Android chats can now hide from prying eyes by default. Only took them until 2026 to catch up with basic privacy expectations.

articles.title: Checkbox Assessments Aren't Fit to Measure to Risk
articles.summary: EFF launches campaign for Saudi Wikipedian Osama Khalid, proving that contributing to human knowledge can still land you in authoritarian crosshairs. Free speech isn't free when dictators hold the invoice.

articles.title: The Science is Not Settled: How Weak Evidence is Fueling a National Push to Ban Social Media for Youth
articles.summary: EFF's Privacy Badger tackles an issue bigger than creepy ads - the complete commodification of human attention and digital autonomy. Because blocking trackers is just the appetizer in the privacy protection feast.
